title: Toyota's Andon Cord: Why Stopping the Line Beats Fixing Mistakes Later
alt_title_1: Taiichi Ohno's 2-Minute Rule That Revolutionized Manufacturing
alt_title_2: Why Any Frontline Worker Could Halt a Toyota Factory
description_hook: In post-war Japan, engineer Taiichi Ohno built the Andon cord into the Toyota Production System: any frontline worker who spotted a single defect pulled an overhead cord to pause the line immediately, trading a two-minute root fix to prevent thousands of defective cars downstream.

scenes.headline: One Overhead Rope Could Halt a Whole Factory
scenes.stat_label: TAIICHI OHNO'S TOYOTA ANDON CORD RULE
bullets: Built in post-war Japan inside the Toyota Production System
Any frontline worker could pause the line on a single defect
scenes.narration: In post-war Japan, Toyota engineer Taiichi Ohno gave every frontline factory worker the authority to freeze an entire assembly line by pulling one overhead rope.
scenes.source: Taiichi Ohno, Toyota Production System (1978; English ed. 1988)

scenes.headline: A 2-Minute Pause Beat Giant Rework Yards
scenes.left_body: Never halts belt -> hides bad bolts -> thousands of defective cars
scenes.right_body: Stops on defect #1 -> 2-minute root fix -> quality compounds
scenes.narration: Old mass-production plants forbade line stops, pushing crooked doors and stripped bolts into giant repair yards out back. Ohno's Andon cord paused work at the very first defect, trading a two-minute source fix to prevent thousands of flawed cars downstream.
scenes.source: Taiichi Ohno, Toyota Production System (1978; English ed. 1988)

scenes.headline: Automation Without a Kill-Switch Scales Garbage
scenes.stat_label: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN BROKEN SCRIPTS RUN UNCHECKED
bullets: Unmonitored AI agents and ad campaigns multiply tiny bugs fast
Chasing non-stop output destroys client trust and cash margin
scenes.narration: Solo operators repeat Detroit's mistake whenever they wire up AI scripts, paid ads, or outreach pipelines without a stop-trigger, multiplying embarrassing errors at machine speed while chasing non-stop volume.
scenes.source: Taiichi Ohno, Toyota Production System (1978; English ed. 1988)

scenes.headline: Wire Automatic Circuit Breakers Into Every Workflow
scenes.stat_label: FIXING ROOT CAUSES EARLY COMPOUNDS CLEAN OUTPUT
scenes.stat_subtext: Hard daily spend caps + anomaly alerts -> zero runaway failures
scenes.narration: Install a hard Andon cord inside every automated system: set strict daily API spend caps, schema checks, and alert triggers that halt execution on anomaly number one.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Taiichi Ohno (1978)

scenes.headline: Stop at Defect One Before It Multiplies
scenes.stat_label: PROTECT REPUTATION AT THE SOURCE, NOT IN REWORK
bullets: Never ship known defects just to hit an arbitrary schedule
Fix the broken step once so tomorrow's line runs cleaner
scenes.narration: Pause the line for two minutes at the very first defect, because fixing root causes early protects years of margin and reputation.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Taiichi Ohno (1978)
